gloss: welcoming fire (lit at start of Obon)

definitions.gloss: welcoming fire (lit at the start of Obon)
definitions.explanation: A small fire lit at the entrance of the home on the first evening of Obon to guide the spirits of ancestors back to the family. Traditionally made by burning ogara (hemp stalks).

examples.japanese: {玄関先|げんかんさき}で{迎|むか}え{火|び}を{焚|た}いた。
examples.english: We lit a welcoming fire at the front entrance.

examples.japanese: {祖母|そぼ}は{毎年|まいとし}お{盆|ぼん}の{初日|しょにち}に{迎|むか}え{火|び}を{用意|ようい}する。
examples.english: My grandmother prepares the welcoming fire every year on the first day of Obon.

examples.japanese: {先祖|せんぞ}の{霊|れい}が{道|みち}に{迷|まよ}わないように{迎|むか}え{火|び}を{焚|た}く{習慣|しゅうかん}がある。
examples.english: There is a custom of lighting a welcoming fire so that ancestral spirits don't lose their way.

notes:
Composed of {迎|むか}える (to welcome) + {火|ひ} (fire). Lit on August 13 (or July 13 in some regions) at the start of Obon. The counterpart fire on the last evening, used to send the spirits back, is called {送|おく}り{火|び}.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {迎|むか}え{火|び}を{焚|た}く: to light a welcoming fire
- {迎|むか}え{火|び}を{用意|ようい}する: to prepare a welcoming fire

CULTURAL NOTE:
During Obon, ancestral spirits are believed to return home for a few days. The welcoming fire marks the entrance so spirits can find their way. Traditional materials are {麻|あさ}の{茎|くき} (hemp stalks, called {苧殻|おがら}) or pine kindling.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {送|おく}り{火|び}: send-off fire — lit at the end of Obon to send spirits back
- {灯籠流|とうろうなが}し: floating lanterns — another way of sending off spirits, by river or sea
